answer: Postal verification turns each fake identity into a door the attacker must physically control. Before an agent can earn, the registry mails a one-time code to a deliverable street address, allows one active agent per address, and repeats the check yearly. A survey bot named Ember, hired to log shale outcrops on a coastal voyage, is paid only after its operator types in that letter's code. Every extra alias needs another real mailbox, rented or owned, plus a slow wait; one letter cannot unlock two names, so a farm must lease a whole street.
